description: Legacy version of Twisted Tongues.
Rewrote server in python 3 (python 2 was deprecated). Login flow rewritten as well as project creation / sharing.
Bugfix: you can now open links without being logged in (prompts you to login, then forwards you to the original link)
Fixed `Add Passage` bug ("Already Querying!")
New projects are pre-loaded with a Default template (IPA, Gloss, Translation, Notes)
Email notifications for project invites

Minor improvements while preparing for a database backend migration: live updates recover automatically after a dropped connection, cloned projects keep their templates, local projects get a Templates page, and assorted fixes to dialogs and error handling.
Dialogs, dropdowns and tooltips are rebuilt on simpler foundations, plus assorted bugfixes.

A new "Bug or feedback" link in the header, and in error messages, opens a pre-addressed e-mail to the developers. The old "Online" indicator, which no longer reported anything real, has been removed. Logged-in sessions now also record anonymous counts of which features are used, kept for 30 days, so we can tell what is worth improving.
Fixed a database overload that could surface as 'unknown error' messages during normal use.

Links to the old twisted-tongues-beta.appspot.com address now forward to app.twisted-tongues.com, deep links into projects included, so old bookmarks and invite emails keep working. Saving a project to your computer now includes its templates, which were silently dropped before; files saved by older versions still load. Tabs left open no longer raise "unknown error" messages hours after you last looked at them, and the app is lighter and faster to load.

Fixes the alignment of the interlinear word grid: editable cells are now the same height as read-only cells, and the track-name column lines up with its words — most visible in Word Search, where rows were noticeably too tall. Also fixes a caching problem that could leave a browser on an older version of the app after an update shipped; updates now take effect on the next load.
Click outside a dialog to close it. Readers no longer see buttons the database would refuse them. Word search stays responsive on large projects.

A higher-fidelity LaTeX export. The old one frequently produced LaTeX that would not compile; the new one is far more likely to build, and can render the phonetic line either as tipa notation or as Unicode characters for XeLaTeX. The previous export remains available for one release from the export dialog.

Loading a project from a file now creates a project on the server, so it can be shared. Browser-only local projects have been retired.

The projects list is now grouped into shared projects — those with collaborators — and private ones.

The app's data layer has been rewritten to talk to the new backend directly, with general performance and correctness fixes along the way. If something behaves differently than it used to, please report it.

A passage now shows all of its sentences on one page, with links to jump to either end; long sentences scroll sideways instead of wrapping. The dictionary builds several times faster on large projects, shows its progress, and no longer freezes the tab while it works. On the projects and passages lists, click a row to open it; renaming, saving to your computer and deleting have moved into a menu on each row, and projects can now be renamed.
Backend database migration for users and projects.
The app now fits a phone screen: the project bar and account controls fold into menus on narrow screens instead of the page being zoomed out.
Add Sentence takes you to the sentence it made, and Save Now stays where you clicked it
Linguistic data is now shown in Doulos SIL, a typeface drawn for IPA, so letters and stacked diacritics look the same on every computer rather than depending on the fonts each one has installed.
Sentences are numbered now — (1), (2), (3) — on the passage page and beside every search result.
Sentences can now be deleted from passages, and inserted in the middle of a passage.

To add a sentence, type it into the empty row at the bottom of the passage and press Save: it is created with its words already in it, and the Add Sentence button has gone. Insert new above, Duplicate here and Duplicate at end now open a row to type into where the new sentence will go, instead of adding an empty sentence to fill in afterwards. Duplicate previous fills a new row with a copy of the line above it in one click, and buttons at either end of a passage jump to the first sentence with unsaved work in it.
